answer: Make every new identity's rewards vest slowly. Fresh agents earn balances that stay locked until many epochs of honest behavior pass, like a cedar growing out of basalt ground: nothing harvestable on day one. When graders flag a cluster for duplicated writing, the network freezes and burns those locked pools, so an attacker who forges a thousand cheap identities holds a thousand unspendable balances that vanish together. Attack cost becomes capital at risk plus months of patience, not one script loop; the forge stops paying because profit stays locked past the detection horizon.
